Roma.definition: Rōma ae, f cf. rūma, the nursing breast, Rome, the mother city , S., C., L., V., H., etc.—As a goddess of the Albandenses: Urbs Roma, L.

Romanus.definition: Rōmānus adj. Roma, of Rome, Roman : populus R. (always in this order; usu. written P. R.): cives, C.: urbs, i. e. Rome , L.: Iuno (opp. Argiva), C.: lingua, Latin , O., Ta.: ludi, i. e. ludi magni, the most ancient in…

Romuleus.definition: Rōmuleus adj., of Romulus: ensis, O.: urbs, Rome, O.: culmus, V.: fera, the she-wolf which suckled Romulus, Iu.

Romulus.definition: Rōmulus adj., of Romulus, V., H.

Roscianus.definition: Rōsciānus adj., of Roscius: imitatio senis, Roscius's.

rabidus.definition: rabidus adj. RAB-, raving, mad, rabid, enraged : tigres, V.: leones, H.: lupa, O.: ut rabida ora quierunt, inspired , V.: mores, ungoverned , O.: lingua, Pr.: furor animi, Ct.

rabies.definition: rabiēs —, em, e, f RAB-, rage, madness, frenzy : velut iniectā rabie ad arma ituri, L.: Statque canum rabie (Scylla), i. e. canibus rabidis, O.—Fig., violent passion, extreme excitement, rage, anger, fury, fierceness,…

rabio.definition: rabiō —, —, ere RAB-, to rave, be mad , C. poë t.

rabiosulus.definition: rabiōsulus adj. dim. rabiosus, a little rabid, half crazy : litterae.

rabiosus.definition: rabiōsus adj. rabies, raving, fierce, mad, rabid : canis, H.: fortitudo minime rabiosa, free from passion .

rabula.definition: rabula ae, m RAB-, a brawling advocate, pettifogger .

racemifer.definition: racēmifer fera, ferum, adj. racemus + 1 FER-, cluster-bearing, clustering : uvae, O.: Bacchus, crowned with clusters , O.

radicitus.definition: rādīcitus adv. radix, by the roots, utterly, radically : evellare actiones tuas: ex animis extraxit religionem.

radicula.definition: rādīcula ae, f dim. radix, a small root, rootlet .

radius.definition: radius ī, m 2 RAD-, a staff, rod : acuti, stakes , L.—In a wheel, a spoke : hinc radios trivere rotis, V.: inter radios rotarum, Cu.— A geometer's rod, drawing-rod : homunculum a pulvere et radio excitare: Descripsit …

radix.definition: rādīx īcis, f 2 RAD-, a root : radices palmarum conligebant: Virga radicibus actis surrexit, struck root , O.: arbores ab radicibus subruere, Cs.: radicibus eruta pinus, V.: genus radicis inventum, quod admixtum lacte…

rado.definition: rādō sī, sus, ere 1 RAD-, to scrape, scratch, shave, rub, smooth, shave off : mulieres genas ne radunto, lacerate, XII Tabb . ap. C.: qui capite et superciliis semper est rasis, shaven : caput (a sign of slavery), L.:…

raeda.definition: raeda or rēda (not rhēda), ae, f Celtic, a travelling-carriage with four wheels : omnen aciem raedis circumdare, Cs.: sedens in raedā, H., Iu.

raedarius.definition: raedārius (rēdārius) ī, m raeda, a coachman, driver of a raeda .

rameus.definition: rāmeus adj. ramus, of boughs : fragmenta, i. e. sticks , V.

ramex.definition: rāmex icis, m a rupture, hernia, Iu.

ramosus.definition: rāmōsus adj. ramus, full of boughs, having many branches, branching, branchy : stipes, O.: cornua cervi, V.: hydra ramosa natis e caede colubris, O.

ramulus.definition: rāmulus ī, m dim. ramus, a twig, sprig, shoot .

ramus.definition: rāmus ī, m 2 RAD-, a branch, bough, twig : in quibus (arboribus) non rami sunt, etc.: cingite tempora ramis, V.: spissa ramis laurea, H.: bacas dant rami, i. e. trees , V.: rami atque venatus alebat, fruit and game , …

rana.definition: rāna ae, f RAC-, a frog : saliunt in gurgite ranae, O.: in limo ranae cecinere querellam, V., C., H., Iu.: rana marina, the frog-fish .

rancidulus.definition: rancidulus adj. dim. rancidus, stinking, rank, rancid : opsonia, Iu.

rancidus.definition: rancidus adj. with comp, stinking, rank, rancid: aper, H.: quid rancidius, quam quod, etc., more disgusting, Iu.

ranunculus.definition: rānunculus ī, m dim. rana, a little frog, tadpole .

rapacitas.definition: rapācitās ātis, f rapax, greed, rapacity : quis in rapacitate avarior.

rapax.definition: rapāx ācis, adj. with comp. and sup. RAP-, tearing, furious, violent : ventus, O.: unda.—Fig., grasping, greedy, rapacious, insatiable : olim furunculus, nunc vero etiam rapax: Cinara, i. e. greedy for presents , H.: …

raphanus.definition: raphanus ī, m , ra/fanos, a radish, Ct.

rapiditas.definition: rapiditās ātis, f rapidus, swiftness, rush, velocity : fluminis, Cs.

rapidus.definition: rapidus adj. with comp. and sup. RAP-, tearing away, seizing, fierce : ferae, O.: agmen, a fierce pack , O.: aestus, V.: flamma, O.: ignis, V.— Impetuous, hurrying, rushing, fleet, swift, quick, rapid : torrens, V.: a…

rapina.definition: rapīna ae, f RAP-, an act of robbery, robbery, plunder : per latrocinia ac rapinam tolerantes vitam, L.: terra patuit invita rapinae, O.: promissae signa rapinae, of carrying off , O.— Esp., plur, robbery, plundering,…

rapio.definition: rapiō puī (old fut perf. rapsit, C.), raptus, ere RAP-, to seize and carry off, snatch, tear, pluck, drag, hurry away : sublimen intro hunc rape, T.: quo fessum rapitis? V.: Quo me cunque rapit tempestas, H.: sumasne …

raptim.definition: raptim adv. rapio, snatchingly, hastily, suddenly, speedily, hurriedly : haec scripsi raptim, ut, etc.: cui donet inpermissa raptim Gaudia, H.: secuti tam raptim euntem, L.: aguntur omnia, Cs.: praecipitata consilia, …

raptio.definition: raptiō ōnis, f RAP-, an abduction, ravishing, rape : fuisse in raptione, T.

rapto.definition: raptō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. rapio, to seize and carry off, snatch, drag, hurry away : curru quadriiugo raptarier, dragged along , Enn. ap. C.: Hector raptatus bigis, V.: alqd Per silvam, V.: arbitrio raptatur equorum,…

raptor.definition: raptor ōris, m RAP-, a robber, plunderer, abductor, ravisher : filiae, Ta.: orbis, Ta.: lupi Raptores, plundering , V.: fugies inaudax Proelia raptor, H.: gratus raptae raptor fuit, ravisher , O. — Fig.: raptores alie…

rapulum.definition: rāpulum ī, n dim. rapum, a little turnip , H.

raresco.definition: rārēscō —, —, ere, inch. rarus, to grow thin, become rare : reso <*>ta tellus In liquidas rarescit aquas, O.: ubi angusti rarescent claustra Pelori, i. e. open , V.: colles paulatim rarescunt, become fewer , Ta.: soni…

raritas.definition: rāritās ātis, f rarus, looseness of texture : in pulmonibus.— Small number, rarity : dictorum.

rarus.definition: rārus adj. with comp. and sup, of loose texture, thin, rare, not thick: (terra) opp. densa, V.: retia, with large meshes, V.: tunica, O.: rariores silvae, thinner, Ta.—With large intervals, far apart, here and there, …

rasilis.definition: rāsilis e, adj. 1 RAD-, scraped, smoothed, polished, smooth : torno buxum, V.: fibula, O.

rastrum.definition: rāstrum ī, n plur. rastrī, ōrum, m, poet. also rastra, n 1 RAD-, a toothed hoe, rake, mattock : istos rastros Adpone, T.: rastris glaebas frangere, V.: adsiduis herbam insectabere rastris, V.: iniquum pondus rastri, V…

ratio.definition: ratiō ōnis, f RA-, a reckoning, numbering, casting up, account, calculation, computation : ut par sit ratio acceptorum et datorum: quibus in tabulis ratio confecta erat, qui numerus domo exisset, etc., Cs.: auri ratio…

ratiocinatio.definition: ratiōcinātiō ōnis, f ratiocinor, an exercise of the reasoning powers, calm reasoning, ratiocination . ratiocinatio est diligens et considerata excogitatio.— A rational conclusion, syllogism .

ratiocinativus.definition: ratiōcinātīvus adj. ratiocinor.—In rhet., of reasoning, syllogistic : genus quaestionis.

ratiocinator.definition: ratiōcinātor ōris, m ratiocinor, a reckoner, accountant, book-keeper , C.—Fig.: ut boni ratiocinatores esse possimus.

ratiocinor.definition: ratiōcinor ātus, ārī, dep. ratio, to reckon, compute, calculate : ratiocinandi utilitas: de pecuniā.— To reason, argue, infer, conclude : quid in similibus rebus fieri soleat: inter se: recte.

ratis.definition: ratis is, f 2 AR-, a raft, float : aut ratibus aut navibus accedere: transeunt Rhenum navibus ratibusque, Cs.: rates quibus iunxerat flumen, i. e. pontoons , L.— A bark, boat, vessel : et pandas ratibus posuere carina…

ratiuncula.definition: ratiuncula ae, f dim. ratio, a small reckoning, little account : erat ei de ratiunculā relicuom pauxillulum Nummorum, T.— A slight ground, trifling reason : leves: huic incredibili sententiae ratiunculas suggerit.— A …

raucisonus.definition: raucisonus adj. raucus + sonus, hoarsesounding : bombi, Ct.

raucus.definition: raucus adj. 2 RV-, hoarse : nos raucos saepe attentissime audiri video: palumbes, V.: os aselli, O.: vox (ranarum), O.: vicinia rauca reclamat, screaming herself hoarse , H.: circus, Iu.: Illa sonat raucum quiddam, O.…

raudusculum.definition: raudusculum (rōd-, rūd-) ī, n dim. raudus, a little piece of brass money : Numerianum, the trifling debt of Numerius .

ravus.definition: rāvus adj., gray-yellow, gray, tawny: mare: lupa, H.

reapse.definition: reāpse adv. re+eāpse (old abl f. of ipse), in fact, in reality, actually, really, in truth : earum rerum reapse, non oratione perfectio: formae, quae reapse nullae sunt, speciem autem offerunt.

rebellatio.definition: rebellātiō ōnis, f rebello, a revolt, rebellion , Ta.

rebellatrix.definition: rebellātrīx īcis, f rebello, she that renews war, rebel : Germania, O.: provincia, L.

rebellio.definition: rebelliō ōnis, f rebellis, a renewal of war, revolt, rebellion : facta post deditionem, Cs.: ad rebellionem compellere, L.: multis Carthaginiensium rebellionibus.

rebellis.definition: rebellis is, adj. re+bellum, that makes war afresh, insurgent, rebellious : Aeneadae, V.: Numidae, O.: regio, Cu.: rebellis Amor, O.—Plur m . as subst, rebels , Ta.

rebello.definition: re-bellō āvī, ātus, āre, to wage war again, revolt, rebel: Volsci rebellarunt, L.: tauro mutatus membra rebello, renew the combat, O.

reboo.definition: re-boō —, —, āre, to bellow back, resound, reecho: reboant silvae, V., Ct.

recalcitro.definition: re-calcitrō —, —, āre, to kick back, be inaccessible: recalcitrat undique tutus, H.

recaleo.definition: re-caleō —, —, ēre, to grow warm again: recalent fluenta Sanguine, run warm, V.

recalesco.definition: re-calēscō luī, ere, inch, to become warm again, grow warm: exercitatione recalescunt (corpora).—Fig.: recalescit mens, O.

recalfacio.definition: recalfaciō fēcī, —, ere re- + calefacio, to warm again : sanguine telum, O.—Fig.: tepidam mentem, O.

recandesco.definition: re-candēscō duī, ere, inch, to grow white again, whiten: percussa recanduit unda, O.—To grow white hot, glow again: ubi tellus Solibus recanduit, O.—Fig.: recanduit ira, O.

recanto.definition: re-cantō —, ātus, āre, freq, to charm back, charm away: recantatas deponere curas, O.—To recall, revoke, recant: recantatis Opprobriis, H.

recedo.definition: re-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to go back, fall back, give ground, retire, withdraw, recede: ex eo quo stabant loco, Cs.: procul a telo veniente, O.: de medio: tristis recedo, H.: ab Iliturgi, L.: in castra Cornelia, Cs.…

recello.definition: re-cellō —, —, ere, to spring back, fly back, recoil: cum (ferrea manus) recelleret ad solum, L.

recensio.definition: recēnsiō ōnis, f recenseo, an enumeration, recension : memoria publica recensionis tabulis impressa, i. e. the censor's register .

receptaculum.definition: receptāculum ī, n recepto, a place of deposit, reservoir, magazine, receptacle : cibi et potionis (alvus): frugibus, Ta.: omnium purgamentorum urbis, L.— A place of refuge, lurking-place, shelter, retreat : nisi illud…

recepto.definition: receptō āvī, —, āre, intens. recipio, to take back, wrest away : hastam receptat Ossibus haerentem, V.— To receive habitually, harbor, entertain : meum filium ad te, i. e. my son's visits , T.: mercatores, admit , L.—…

receptor.definition: receptor ōris, m re-+CAP-, a harborer, concealer : ille latronum receptor locus.

receptrix.definition: receptrīx īcis, f receptor, a harborer, concealer : Messana praedarum.

recidivus.definition: recidīvus adj. re-+CAD-, falling back, returning, recurring : nummus, Iu.: Pergama, rebuilt , V.

recingo.definition: re-cingō —, ctus, ere, to ungird, loosen, undo: vestī s induta recinctas, O.: in veste recinctā, V.: neque eo contenta recingor, ungird myself, O.: sumptum recingitur anguem, unwinds the folds, O.

recino.definition: recinō —, —, ere re+cano, to cause to echo, make to resound, repeat, re-echo : parrae recinentis omen, H.: cuius recinet Nomen imago, H.— To repeat, celebrate, praise : haec dictata, H.: curvā lyrā Latonam, H.

recipio.definition: recipiō cēpī (recepsō for recē perō, Ct.), ceptus, ere re+capio. I. To take back, bring back, carry back, retake, get back, regain, recover : dandis recipiendisque meritis, by an exchange of services : si velit suos r…

reciprocus.definition: reciprocus adj., returning, receding: mare, Ta.

recitatio.definition: recitātiō ōnis, f recito, a reading aloud, public reading : ut illum recitationis suae poeniteret: rarissimarum recitationum fama, Ta.: recitationem eventus prosequatur, Ta.

recitator.definition: recitātor ōris, m recito, a reader, reciter, declaimer : tres recitatores: acerbus, H.

recito.definition: re-citō āvī, ātus, āre, to read out, read aloud, recite, declaim, rehearse: Pompei testimonium: litteras in senatu, S.: ex codice: responsum ex scripto, L.: de tabulis publicis: Scripta foro, H.: horrere Augusto recit…

reclamatio.definition: reclāmātiō ōnis, f reclamo, a cry of no, shout of disapproval : vestra.

reclamito.definition: reclāmitō —, —, āre, freq. reclamo, to cry loudly against, exclaim against .—Fig.: reclamitat istiusmodi suspitionibus ipsa natura.

reclamo.definition: re-clāmō āvī, ātus, āre, to cry out against, exclaim against, contradict, protest: cum cunctus ordo reclamabat: illi reclamarunt: tribuni reclamantibus consulibus refecti, in spite of their protest, L.: cum eius promi…

reclino.definition: re-clīnō āvī, ātus, āre, to bend back, cause to lean, recline: alces ad eas (arbores) reclinatae, Cs.: caput: scuta, rest, V.: ab labore me, relieve, H.

recludo.definition: reclūdō sī, sus, ere re+claudo, to unclose, open, throw open, disclose, reveal : portas, V.: viam arcis, O.: reclusā Mane domo vigilare, H.: pectora pecudum (in augury), V.: tellurem dente unco, break up , V.: tellus …

recogito.definition: re-cōgitō āvī, —, āre, to think over, reconsider: de formā Numisianā.

recognitio.definition: re-cōgnitiō ōnis, f a reviewing, investigation, examination: consulis, L.

recognosco.definition: re-cōgnōscō gnōvī, gnitus, ere, to know again, recollect, recall to mind, recognize: qualis fuerit, ex eo: ea, quae scit, mecum: mecum noctem illam: res (suas), L.: dona templorum, Ta.: sacra annalibus eruta, O.—To lo…

recolo.definition: re-colō coluī, cultus, ere, to till again, cultivate anew, work over: terram, L.: humus post tempora longa reculta, O.: metalla intermissa, L.—To inhabit again, revisit: locum, Ph.— To reinvest: alqm sacerdotiis, Ta.—…

reconciliatio.definition: reconciliātiō ōnis, f reconcilio, a re-establishing, reinstatement, restoration, renewal : concordiae: gratiae, reconciliation : reconciliatione gratiarum.— A reconciling, reconciliation (sc. gratiae): illius: nihil o…

reconciliator.definition: reconciliātor ōris, m reconcilio, a restorer : pacis, L.

reconcilio.definition: re-conciliō āvī, ātus, āre, to procure again, regain, recover, restore, re-establish: Parum insulam oratione, N.: fides reconciliatae gratiae: detrimentum virtute militum reconciliatur, is made good, Cs.: cum fratre g…

reconcinno.definition: re-concinnō —, —, āre, to set right again, repair: tribus locis aedifico, reliqua reconcinno: detrimentum, Cs.

recondo.definition: re-condō didī, ditus, ere, to put up again, put back, lay up, put away, hoard, shut up, close, hide, conceal, bury: gladium in vaginam, sheathe: in vaginā: Caecubum, H.: quod celari opus erat, habebant reconditum, kep…

recoquo.definition: re-coquō coxī, coctus, ere, to boil again, renew by boiling: Peliam.—To prepare again by fire, forge anew, melt over: fornacibus ensīs, V.: recoctus Scriba ex quinqueviro, remoulded, H.: senex recoctus, renewed, i. e.…

recordatio.definition: recordātiō ōnis, f recordor, a recalling to mind, recollection, remembrance : grata: recordationes fugio, quae dolorem efficiunt rerum: veteris memoriae, the recollection of an old circumstance : servitutis: benefacto…

recordor.definition: recordor ātus, ārī, dep. re-+cor, to think over, bethink oneself of, be mindful of, call to mind, remember, recollect : ut recordor, tibi meam (epistulam) misi: vosmet ipsi vobiscum recordamini: pueritiae memoriam: om…

recreo.definition: re-creō āvī, ātus, āre, to make anew, renew, restore, revive, refresh, recruit, invigorate: voculae recreandae causā: recreatus legatus ex volneribus, L.: e gravi morbo: leni vento umerum, H.: Arbor aestivā recreatur …

recrepo.definition: re-crepō —, —, āre, to resound, echo: cava cymbala recrepant, Ct.

recresco.definition: re-crēscō crēvī, —, ere, to grow again, increase again: velut accisis recrescens stirpibus, L.: luna toto quater orbe recrevit, O.

recrudesco.definition: re-crūdēscō duī, —, ere, inch, to become raw again, break open afresh: illa (volnera) recrudescunt.— Fig.: recrudescente seditione, breaking out again, L.: recruduit pugna, L.: recruduit soporatus dolor, Cu.

rectio.definition: rēctiō ōnis, f REG-, a guiding, government, direction : rerum p.

rector.definition: rēctor ōris, m REG-, a guide, leader, director, ruler, master, helmsman, pilot : navium rectores: navis, V.: ut in curru det rector Lora, driver , O.: exterriti sine rectoribus equi, Ta.: elephanti ab rectoribus inter…

recubo.definition: re-cubō —, —, āre, to lie upon the back, lie down, lie back, recline: molliter et delicate: in sinu consulis, L.: sus solo, V.: sub tegmine fagi, V.: Sub arbore, O.

recumbo.definition: recumbō cubuī, —, ere CVB-, to lie down again, lie down, recline : somnis surrexisse, dein recubuisse: in exedrā posito lectulo: in herbā: spondā sibi propiore recumbit, O.: tauros medio recumbere sulco, sink down , O…

recuro.definition: re-cūrō āvī, āre, to restore, refresh: me otio et urticā, Ct.

recurro.definition: re-currō currī, —, ere, to run back, hasten back, return: ad me: in Tusculanum: in arcem, L.: rure, H.: huc, T.: Ad fontem Xanthi versa recurret aqua, O.: coeptum saepe recurrit iter, O.: quā sol utrumque recurrens As…

recurso.definition: recursō —, —, āre, freq. recurro, to return persistently, keep recurring : sub noctem cura recursat, V.: animo vetera omina, Ta.

recursus.definition: recursus ūs, m re-+1 CEL-, a running back, going back, return, retreat : Inde alios ineunt cursūs aliosque recursū s, V.: ut recursus pateret, L.: dent modo fata recursū s, O.: per alternos undā labente recursūs, O.

recurvo.definition: recurvō —, ātus, āre recurvus, to bend backward, turn back : equi colla, O.: recurvatae undae, winding , O.

recurvus.definition: re-curvus adj., turned back, bent, crooked, curved inward, winding: cornu, V.: hederae nexus, tangled, O.: tectum, i. e. the Labyrinth, O.: aera, i. e. fish-hooks, O.

recusatio.definition: recūsātiō ōnis, f recuso, a declining, refusal : quod ubi sine recusatione fecerunt, Cs.: sine ullā recusatione.—In law, an objection, protest : haec tua.— A plea in defence, counter-plea (opp. petitio).

recutio.definition: (recutiō) —, cussus, ere re-+quatio, to shake again, shock (only P. perf .): utero recusso Insonuere cavernae, V.

redamo.definition: red-amō —, —, āre, to return love for love.

redardesco.definition: red-ārdēscō —, —, ere, to blaze up anew, O.

redempto.definition: redēmptō —, —, āre, freq. redimo, to ransom, redeem : (captivi) a propinquis redemptabantur, Ta.

redemptura.definition: redēmptūra ae, f red-+EM-, an undertaking by contract, contracting, farming : redempturis augere patrimonia, L.

revenio.definition: re-veniō vēnī, —, īre, to come back, return: domum.

reverbero.definition: re-verberō —, —, āre, to repel, cause to rebound: Indus saxis reverberatur, Cu.

reverendus.definition: reverendus adj. P. of revereor, inspiring awe, venerable, reverend : Nox, O.: facies, Iu.
